claims.text: Defense Intelligence Reference Document titled "MHD Air Breathing Propulsion and Power for Aerospace Applications", series "Defense Futures", published 2010-11-21 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date (ICOD) of 2010-07-20, DIA document number DIA-08-1011-006. Released by DIA under FOIA and posted in the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room.

Inside cover reads: "This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted b(3) 10 USC 424] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program" and directs questions to the "AAWSA Program Manager, Defense Intelligence Agency, ATTN: [redacted], Bldg 6000, Washington, DC 20340-5100".

Author name is withheld in the DIA-released copy under FOIA exemption (b)(6); the "Prepared by:" line is withheld under (b)(3) 10 USC 424. The released cover therefore does not attribute the DIRD to a named author.

claims.text: ITS OWN SUMMARY, VERBATIM, and it is a document about hypersonic aerodynamics and nothing else: 'The paper reviews novel propulsion concepts utilizing plasmas (ionized gases) and magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). These concepts are shown to be attractive due to their potential to achieve propulsion and aerodynamic performance far beyond current conventional technologies. However, significant difficulties impede the development and application of these technologies; these include weight, complexity, higher power, and the need for complex and energy-consuming artificial ionization in "cold" air (at Mach <12).'

claims.text: Its finding on the concept the popular literature most often reaches for, verbatim: 'A well-publicized Ajax concept of MHD energy bypass has been shown to be meaningless below at least Mach 12. In contrast, a new "reverse energy bypass" with Virtual Cowl is potentially practical for air-breathing hypersonic vehicles.'

The word 'gravity' occurs once. Its chapter structure is concept overview, aeronautical applications, space applications, and summary and predictions, with figures on arcjet thrusters, gridded ion thrusters, Hall thrusters, scramjet inlet control by e-beam ionization, the Ajax vehicle concept, the virtual cowl and reentry drag reduction.

claims.text: Stated inference, and it is the strand's comparison. The board already records that this DIRD is attributed on the DIA list supplied to the Senate Armed Services Committee to 'Dr S Macheret, Lockheed Martin'. A government agency paid a Lockheed Martin plasma physicist to survey magnetohydrodynamic propulsion under the same programme the lore invokes, and what he delivered concerns scramjet inlets, virtual cowls and reentry drag reduction. NOTHING JOINS THIS DOCUMENT TO US 3,322,374 and the edge between them records a similarity of subject only.

Cover page reads: '21 November 2010 / ICOD: 20 July 2010 / DIA-08-1011-006 / Defense Intelligence Reference Document / Defense Futures / MHD Air Breathing Propulsion and Power for Aerospace Applications'.

dossier.narrative:
The value of this document to the board is that it is boring, and that its boringness is checkable.

Its own summary describes a review of 'novel propulsion concepts utilizing plasmas (ionized gases) and magnetohydrodynamics', and its assessment is unflattering: the concepts face significant difficulties of weight, complexity and higher power. On the specific concept the popular literature reaches for most, it is blunter still, finding that the well-publicised Ajax MHD energy-bypass concept 'has been shown to be meaningless below at least Mach 12'.

The zero-counts over the whole released 33-page PDF, taken 19 September 2026: **UFO 0, unidentified 0, anti-gravity 0, antigravity 0, scalar 0, zero point 0, levitation 0.** The word 'gravity' occurs only in ordinary aerodynamic senses.

Read beside King's 1967 patent, which claims exactly MHD with an atmosphere as its armature and mentions scalar, spin and gravity zero times, and beside Yamato-1, which put superconducting MHD to sea at Kobe in 1992 and performed poorly, this document completes a picture the strand exists to draw. The mechanism is real, it was patented, it was built, it was assessed by the government, and at no point in that chain does anything exotic appear. The exotic content arrives only when the mechanism is invoked rather than examined.

The released copy is 33 pages, with the author withheld under the same two exemptions.
dossier.whyImplicated: Magnetohydrodynamics is the mechanism the lore most often reaches for when it wants a propulsion story that sounds technical, and this is the government's own assessment of it. It sits in the propulsion strand as the document that shows what a real MHD review looks like: hypersonic aerodynamics, weight, complexity and power budgets, with no exotic content anywhere.
